problem: Prior supervised vision and motion perception systems are built separately with limited skills (passive VO or localization), and RL navigation systems in real environments rely on noisy GPS labels, vision-only inputs, and many training episodes, with unexplored generalization to lighting or weather changes.
motivation: Long-term, all-weather outdoor navigation requires robust perception that does not depend on unreliable GPS across month-spaced traversals. The paper observes that compact motion (VO) and visual place features, both obtainable via self-supervision from a single image sequence, are complementary: motion is invariant to appearance change while vision disambiguates places.
key_idea: Temporally fuse self-supervised VO motion states (SS-DPC-Net) and self-supervised visual place representations (SFRS) as compact inputs to a PPO-trained LSTM policy for goal-driven navigation on real driving data.
insight: Motion+vision together beats either alone: on Oxford RobotCar the full model needed about 15k training episodes vs 60k (motion-only) and 44k (vision-only), and generalized from day to night at ~80% success vs ~30% for vision-only. On KITTI, the motion-only baseline is competitive because deployment is on the training traversal, so vision only matters under appearance change. The paper also studies the trade-off between VO precision and RL success rate.
method: Self-supervised visual localization: SFRS (self-supervised fine-grained region similarities) provides compact visual observation features x_t from monocular images, robust to noisy GPS labels.
Self-supervised monocular VO: SS-DPC-Net combines depth estimation, optical flow and classical VO to give compact ego-motion states m_t.

Policy network: a 512-unit linear layer encodes m_t and x_t, then a 256-unit LSTM combines them with the previous action a_{t-1} and outputs actions and value V (architecture inspired by Mirowski et al. NIPS 2018).
RL training: PPO with discrete actions, sparse reward (+1 only on reaching the target) and multi-level curriculum learning to encourage exploration.
Environment: CityLearn interactive framework built on KITTI and Oxford RobotCar single traversals; the baselines are motion-only and vision-only variants of the same setup.

setting.backbone: SFRS visual encoder + SS-DPC-Net VO (self-supervised, pretrained) + LSTM policy trained with PPO
setting.training_data: Single traversal of KITTI (sequence 05) and Oxford RobotCar images; self-supervised perception plus RL episodes in CityLearn (tens of thousands of episodes)
setting.observation: monocular RGB image sequence converted to compact motion and visual features (no GPS at input)
setting.action_space: discrete actions along the traversal in CityLearn
setting.simulator: CityLearn (built on real KITTI and Oxford RobotCar datasets)
setting.privileged: none (GT odometry used only for analysis of VO precision)

numbers.eval_set_note: trained and tested on KITTI sequence 05 of the raw data
numbers.extra: deployed on the same traversal used for training; results averaged over 6 seeds for training curves
numbers.evidence: For the KITTI dataset, our full model can solve navigation tasks with 80% success rate, compared to 65% for the vision-only system.

numbers.extra: trained on day traversal, deployed at night
numbers.evidence: our full model is capable of consistently obtaining around an 80% success rate, compared to 30% for the vision-only system.

numbers_note: Results are mostly in figures (training curves, deployment statistics); only the headline success rates are stated in text. The 80% Oxford value is approximate ('around').
results: On KITTI the full model reaches 80% SR vs 65% for vision-only, while motion-only is competitive. On Oxford RobotCar under day-to-night change it gets ~80% SR vs ~30% for vision-only, and it trains in 15k episodes vs 60k (motion-only) and 44k (vision-only).
limitations: Evaluated only on single fixed traversals of driving datasets in a simulated CityLearn framework, with no real robot deployment and little quantitative reporting (mostly figures).
Deployment on the training route on KITTI means the results do not test generalization there, so motion-only appears competitive.
Perception is pretrained and fused with RL; the paper leaves fully unsupervised decision-making for future work.
builds_on: Mirowski et al. 2018 (learning to navigate in cities without a map)
